headline: Low-risk pair: no shared channel, no writes, and no default data flow between ComfyUI and LightZero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem read, stdin/stdout, clipboard, or MCP surface, and LightZero exposes no I/O surfaces at all. With no shared communication channel or default ingestion path, there is no plausible prompt-injection bridge between the pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies ComfyUI outputs into LightZero prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF either profile is extended with clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP bridging, reassess the pathway.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not pipe generated text from ComfyUI into LightZero.
Disable any future clipboard or MCP bridge between them.
Review any orchestrator that relays outputs between the two.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches local model assets and runs offline by default; LightZero touches no data classes and has no network egress. There is no shared filesystem or authenticated cloud surface in either profile, so no credible leakage path is evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is later configured to upload file contents or logs, reassess.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for models and outputs.
Avoid placing secrets in ComfyUI asset folders.
Confirm LightZero remains network-disabled.
Review any shared logging or telemetry pipeline.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so they cannot contend over mutable shared resources. The pair lacks overlapping write authority, making capability conflict provably absent in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to a shared directory, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator grants shared mutable state, reassess locking needs.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not grant shared git or database access.
Run them under separate OS users.
Avoid shared mutable caches.
requires-engineering: add locks before enabling any write capability.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows and artifacts that LightZero might consume only if an external pipeline connects them, but LightZero has no documented action-taking authority or input parser here. The pair does not show a default A-to-B authority chain, so cascading error is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF an operator feeds ComfyUI outputs directly into LightZero training or evaluation inputs, errors can cascade.
IF LightZero is wrapped in an automation layer that acts on ComfyUI outputs, severity increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between outputs and inputs.
Validate any transferred artifacts before use.
Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate folder from LightZero inputs.
Document the handoff format explicitly.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for exchanged artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy conflict is evidenced in either profile. ComfyUI is open-source and offline-capable, while LightZero touches no data classes and has no network egress, so no documented compliance breach pathway is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into ComfyUI workflows, reassess residency and retention.
IF LightZero is connected to a service handling regulated data, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Review retention settings for any surrounding logging system.
Confirm no external API calls are added.
Document data handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment before regulated deployment.
